_meta.source: Federal Statistical Office (BFS) — population figures are approximate, rounded to the latest available annual estimate.
_meta.note: NC seats = number of National Council seats apportioned to the canton by population.

ZH.name: Zürich
ZH.desc: The most populous canton and economic engine of Switzerland, home to the largest city and a major global financial centre.

BE.name: Bern
BE.desc: The second largest canton by area and host of the federal city. Bern is bilingual and politically diverse.

LU.name: Luzern
LU.desc: A central Swiss canton known for lake and mountain tourism, historically Catholic and Centre-leaning.

UR.name: Uri
UR.desc: One of the three founding cantons of the Swiss Confederation in 1291, at the heart of the Gotthard route.

SZ.name: Schwyz
SZ.desc: The canton from which Switzerland takes its name, and a founding member of the original confederation.

OW.name: Obwalden
OW.desc: A half-canton of Unterwalden, known for a low flat tax rate that has attracted businesses.

NW.name: Nidwalden
NW.desc: The second half-canton of Unterwalden, small but historically significant as a founding community.

GL.name: Glarus
GL.desc: Known for its Landsgemeinde, an open-air assembly where citizens still vote by show of hands.

ZG.name: Zug
ZG.desc: One of the wealthiest cantons per capita, a hub for international corporations and blockchain firms.

FR.name: Fribourg
FR.desc: A bilingual canton straddling the French-German language border (Röstigraben), historically Catholic.

SO.name: Solothurn
SO.desc: Home to a striking Baroque old town, Solothurn has a rich historical and cultural heritage.

BS.name: Basel-Stadt
BS.desc: The smallest canton by area, Basel-Stadt is a pharmaceutical and cultural hub on the Rhine.

BL.name: Basel-Landschaft
BL.desc: Surrounding Basel-Stadt, this canton split off in 1832 and is home to many pharmaceutical workers.

SH.name: Schaffhausen
SH.desc: The northernmost canton, famous for the Rhine Falls, Europe's most powerful waterfall by volume.

AR.name: Appenzell Ausserrhoden
AR.desc: The Protestant half of Appenzell, known for embroidery and rolling pre-Alpine hills.

AI.name: Appenzell Innerrhoden
AI.desc: The smallest canton by population, and the last in Switzerland to grant women the cantonal vote, in 1990 by court order.

SG.name: St. Gallen
SG.desc: Historically known for its abbey and textile industry, today a major economic region of eastern Switzerland.

GR.name: Graubünden
GR.desc: The largest canton by area and Switzerland's only trilingual canton, home to St. Moritz and Davos.

AG.name: Aargau
AG.desc: A populous industrial canton in the Swiss heartland, known for its castles and Roman heritage at Vindonissa.

TG.name: Thurgau
TG.desc: An agricultural and industrial canton on Lake Constance, with a strong tradition of apple growing.

TI.name: Ticino
TI.desc: Switzerland's only Italian-speaking canton, south of the Alps, with a Mediterranean character.

VD.name: Vaud
VD.desc: The second most populous canton, home to Lausanne, Lake Geneva's northern shore and many international bodies.

VS.name: Valais
VS.desc: A bilingual mountain canton containing the highest Swiss Alpine peaks, including the Matterhorn.

NE.name: Neuchâtel
NE.desc: A centre of Swiss watchmaking, with a rich horological heritage along the Jura arc.

GE.name: Geneva
GE.desc: An international city and canton, home to UN agencies, the Red Cross and a cosmopolitan diplomatic community.

JU.name: Jura
JU.desc: Switzerland's youngest canton, created in 1979 after a decades-long autonomy movement from Bern.
